senses.gloss:
दर दर, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. दॄ; at the end
of comp.) cleaving, rending, splitting, cutting open,
opening, breaking [cf. पुरन्-द्˚]; (अस्, अम्), m.
f. n. a hole in the ground, a cave, cavity; a conch-
shell; (ई), f. a natural or artificial excavation in a
mountain, a cave, a cavern, a grotto, &c.; a valley;
(अस्), m. a stream [cf. असृग्-द्˚]; fear, terror, dread,
despair; (अस्, आ, अम्), little, small; (अम्), ind. a
little.
—दर-कण्टिका, f. the plant Asparagus Race-
mosa (= शतावरी).
—दर-तिमिर, अम्, n. the
[]
darkness of fear.
—दर-मन्थर, अस्, आ, अम्, a
little slow.
—दर-मुकुलित, अस्, आ, अम्, a little
budded.
—दर-विदलित, अस्, आ, अम्, slightly burst
or opened.
—दर-व्रीडा, f. slight shame.
—दर-
श्लथ, अस्, आ, अम्, a little loose.
—दरी-भू, ऊस्, f.
a cavern, a hollow.
—दरी-भृत्, त्, m. ‘having
caves,’ a mountain.
—दरी-मुख, अम्, n. a mouth
like a cave; a cave like a mouth; the opening of
a cave; (अस्, ई, अम्), having a mouth as large as a
cave; (अस्), m., N. of a monkey.
—दरी-वत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, containing caves, cavernous, abounding in
caves.
—दरेन्द्र (˚र-इन्˚), अस्, m. Viṣṇu's conch.

दार दार, अस्, m. (fr. rt. दॄ), a rent, cleft,
gap, hole; a ploughed field; a wife, (usually occurring
in the m. pl. आस् or in comp.: an exceptional form दारा,
f. sing., occurs in one or two passages; and in Pañca-
tantra I. 450, the neut. pl. दाराणि); दारान् कृ, to
take a wife, marry; [cf. कृत-द्˚.]
—दार-कर्-
मन्, अ, n. or दार-क्रिया, f. taking a wife, marry-
ing, marriage; [cf. दार-परिग्रह.]
—दार-
गव, अम्, n. wife and cows.
—दार-ग्रहण, अम्,
n. ‘taking a wife,’ marriage.
—दार-परिग्रह,
अस्, m. ‘taking a wife,’ marriage.
—दारपरिग्र-
हिन्, ई, इणी, इ, ‘taking a wife,’ marrying.
—दार-
लक्षण, अम्, n. a characteristic sign or decisive
mark of wife-hood.
—दार-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘taking
a wife,’ marrying, marriage.
—दाराणुक्रमण
(˚र-अण्˚), अम्, n., N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-
sarva-sva.
—दाराधीन (˚र-अध्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
dependent on a wife, in the power of a wife.
—दा-
रोपसङ्ग्रह (˚र-उप्˚), अस्, m. ‘taking a wife,’
marrying, marriage.

दार; the meaning ‘a ploughed field’ to be
erased; the words printed एकके दारे in Manu IX.
38. should be एक-केदारे, (see केदार.)

दरण, अम्, n. the act of cleaving, rending,
splitting, tearing, breaking; breaking off, falling
away.

दारण, अस्, ई, अम्, tearing, splitting, tearing
asunder; (ई), f. an epithet of Durgā; (अम्), n. the
act of tearing, rending, dividing; opening, bursting,
[]
flying open; a means of opening; the clearing-nut
plant, Strychnos Potatorum; [cf. कतक.]

दरणि, इस्, इस्, m. f. breaking; an eddy; a cur-
rent; breakers, surf.

दरथ, अस्, m. a cavity, cave; running away,
taking flight; spreading over the country for forage.

दरद, आस्, m. pl. a country bordering on
Kaśmīr, the mountains about Kaśmīr and above
Peshāwar; the inhabitants of this country; (अस्), m.
the king or chief of the Daradas; (अस्), m. fear,
terror; (अम्), n. red lead.

दारद दारद, अस्, ई, अम्, coming from
the country of the Darads, (a various reading has
दरद); (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people, (probably
only a wrong form for दरद); (अस्), m. a kind of
poison brought from the above country; quicksilver;
the ocean; (अस्, अम्), m. n. vermilion.

दरि, इस्, इस्, इ, splitting, rending, opening [cf.
गो-द्˚]; (इस्), m., N. of a Nāga; (इस्), f. a cave.
(For दरी see under दर.)

दारि, इस्, इस्, इ, tearing, causing to burst, splitting
[cf. वेणु-द्˚]; (इस्), f. cutting, tearing, dividing.
दारी, f. a cleft, gap; a chap.

दरित, अस्, आ, अम्, frightened, terrified, timid;
torn, rent, divided.
दारित, अस्, आ, अम्, torn, rent, divided.
दारित दारित, &c. See col. 1.

दर्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, or दर्त्नु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved.
a breaker, render, splitting, breaking, one who splits,
breaks, or opens.

दर्दर, अस्, आ, अम्, cracked, broken, burst,
flawed, slightly broken; (अस्), m. a mountain (‘con-
taining caves’); N. of a mountain (also दर्दुर);
a kind of drum.
—दर्दराम्र (˚र-आम्˚), अस्, m.
a sort of sauce or condiment (= मीनाम्रीण).

दर्दर दर्दर, दर्दरीक, दर्दुर. See
last col.

दर्दरीक, अस्, m. a frog; a cloud; a kind of
musical instrument; (अम्), n. any musical instru-
ment; [cf. दर्वरीक.]

दर्दुर, अस्, m. (perhaps an onomatopoetic
word), a frog [cf. दार्दुर and दार्दुरिक]; a sort
of musical instrument, a pipe or flute; the sound of
a drum; a cloud; a sort of rice; a mountain; N.
of a mountain in the south (sometimes associated with
the mountain Malaya); N. of a man; of a gamester;
(आ or ई), f. a N. of Durgā; (अम्), n. an assem-
blage of villages, a district, a province.
—दर्दुर-
च्छदा, f. or दर्दुर-पर्णी, f., N. of a plant, =
ब्राह्मी.
—दर्दुर-पुट, अस्, m. the mouth or
extremity of a pipe.

दार्दुर दार्दुर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दर्दुर), re-
lating to a cloud, frog, &c.; (अम्), n. a conch-shell
or muscle, the valve of which opens to the right;
lac; water.

दर्दुरक, अस्, m., N. of a gamester; [cf. द-
रोदर and दुरोदर.]

दर्दू, ऊस्, or दर्द्रु, उस्, or दर्द्रू, ऊस्, m.
(according to some fr. दरिद्रा), = दद्रु, cutaneous
and herpetic eruptions, especially a kind of leprosy.
—दर्द्रु-घ्न, अस्, m. = दद्रु-घ्न, the shrub
Cassia Tora; Psoralea Corylifolia.
—दर्द्रु-नाशिनी,
f. a kind of insect, = तैलिनी.
—दर्द्रु-रोगिन् or
दर्द्रू-रोगिन्, ई, इणी, इ, afflicted with cutaneous
eruptions, herpetic.

दर्द्रुण or दर्द्रूण, अस्, आ, अम्, having cu-
taneous eruptions, herpetic.

दरिद्रा दरिद्रा (reduplicated form of
rt. 1. द्रा; according to some, an old
Intens. form; perhaps connected with rt. दॄ), cl. 2.
P. दरिद्राति (दरिद्रिवस्, दरिद्रितस्, 3rd pl. द-
रिद्रति), दरिद्राञ्-चकार or ददरिद्रौ, दरि-
द्रिष्यति, अदरिद्रीत् and अदरिद्रासीत्, दरिद्रि-
तुम्, to be poor or needy, to be in distress.

दरिद्र, अस्, आ, अम्, poor, needy, indigent, dis-
tressed, a poor person, beggar; (Ved.) unsteady,
roving, strolling.
—दरिद्र-ता, f. or दरिद्र-त्व,
अम्, n. poverty, indigence, penury.
—दरिद्र-
निन्दा, f., N. of the twenty-fifth chapter of the
Śārṅgadhara-paddhati.

दारिद्र दारिद्र, अम्, n. (fr. दरिद्र), poverty,
indigence, (perhaps a wrong form for दारिद्र्य
below.)

दरिद्राण, अम्, n. the state of being poor,
poverty.
दरिद्रायक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, poor, needy.
दरिद्रित, अस्, आ, अम्, impoverished, distressed.
दरिद्रितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, poor, distressed, needy.

दरोदर दरोदर, अस्, m. = दुरोदर, a
gamester [cf. दर्दुर and दर्दुरक]; a stake
at play; (अम्), n. gambling, playing at dice; a
die, dice.

दारोदर दारोदर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दरोदर),
connected with gambling.

दर्प दर्प, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 3. दृप् or 2. दृप्;
according to some, also अम्, n.), pride, arrogance,
haughtiness, insolence, rashness, temerity; vanity, con-
ceit; sullenness, sulkiness; Pride &c. personified as a
son of Śrī, or of A-dharma and Śrī, or of Dharma and
Lakṣmī, or of Unnati; heat; musk; [cf. अति-द्˚
and स-द्˚.]
—दर्प-च्छिद्, त्, त्, त्, destroying pride,
humbling.
—दर्प-द, अस्, m., N. of Śiva.
—दर्-
प-ध्मात, अस्, आ, अम्, puffed up or swelling with
pride.
—दर्प-नारायण, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—दर्प-पत्त्रक, अस्, m. a kind of grass; [cf. दर्-
भ-पत्त्र.]
—दर्प-पूर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, full of
pride.
—दर्प-सार, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—दर्-
प-ह or दर्प-हर, अस्, आ, अम्, pride-destroying,
humbling, humiliating.
—दर्प-हन्, आ, m., N. of
Śiva.
—दर्पारम्भ (˚प-आर्˚), अस्, m. beginning
of pride, incipient pride, conceit.
—दर्पोपशान्ति
(˚प-उप्˚), इस्, f. allaying pride, conciliating or sub-
duing arrogance.

दर्पक, अस्, आ, अम्, making proud, inflaming,
exciting, an inflamer; (अस्), m. a N. of Kāma-deva,
god of love.

दर्पण, अस्, m. ‘causing vanity or pride,’ a
looking-glass, mirror, (sometimes occurring at the
end of comp. or titles of books, e. g. कर्ण-द्˚,
ज्ञान-द्˚, साहित्य-द्˚, q. v.); a N. of Śiva [cf.
दर्प-द]; N. of a mountain inhabited by Kuvera
and of a river rising there; (अम्), n. the eye;
kindling, inflaming.

दर्पित, अस्, आ, अम्, made proud, arrogant; in-
flamed.
—दर्पित-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town.
दर्पिन्, ई, इणी, इ, proud, arrogant, insolent.

दर्भ दर्भ, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. दृभ्; said
to be fr. rt. दॄ), a bundle of grass, tuft or bunch
of grass; N. of various kinds of grass used at sacri-
ficial ceremonies, especially of the Kuśa grass, Poa
Cynosuroides; Saccharum Spontaneum; Saccharum
Cylindricum; (the first kind or Kuśa grass was held
very sacred; it was used to strew the ground in
preparing for a sacrifice, the officiating Brāhmans
being purified by sitting on it; under the name Darbha
it was even addressed as a deity; its various sancti-
fying qualities are described in Manu II. 43, III.
208, IV. 36, &c.; cf. कुश, काश, मुञ्ज, वल्व-ज,
शर); N. of a man; [cf. Old Germ. zurba, zurft;
Mod. Germ. torf; Eng. turf.]
—दर्भ-कुसुम,
अस्, m. a kind of insect (= दर्भ-पुष्प).
—दर्-
भ-चीर, अम्, n. a dress of Kuśa grass.
—दर्भ-त-
रुणक, अम्, n., Ved. a young shoot of Kuśa grass.
—दर्भ-पत्त्र, अस्, m. a kind of grass, Saccha-
rum Spontaneum (= काश).
—दर्भ-पुञ्जील =
दर्भ-पिञ्जूल, अम्, n., Ved. a bunch or bundle
of Kuśa grass.
—दर्भ-पुष्प, अस्, m. a kind of
serpent; a kind of insect, ‘similar to the Darbha
flower;’ [cf. दर्भ-कुसुम.]
—दर्भ-मय,
अस्, ई, अम्, made of Kuśa or Darbha grass.
—दर्भ-
मुष्टि, इस्, m. f. a handful of Kuśa grass.
—दर्भ-
संस्तर, अस्, m. a bed of Darbha grass.
—दर्भ-
स्तम्ब, अस्, m. a cluster or bunch of Kuśa grass.
—दर्भाह्वय (˚भ-आह्˚), अस्, m. a kind of
grass; [cf. मुञ्ज.]
दर्भ, अस्, m. See p. 403, col. 2.

दार्भ दार्भ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दर्भ), made
of Darbha grass.

दर्भर, अस्, m. (?), a kind of bird, = लावा,
Perdix Chinensis.
दर्भि, इस्, m. or दर्भिन्, ई, m., N. of a man.

दार्भि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Darbha; (see
Pāṇ. IV. 1, 102.)

दर्भट दर्भट, अम्, n. a private apartment
or house, a retired room; [cf. दार्वट.]

दर्वट, अस्, m. a door-keeper, warder, village
constable, police officer; [cf. गर्वाट.]
दर्वट दर्वट. See above.

दार्वट दार्वट, अम्, n. (fr. the Pers. دربار),
a court or council-house; [cf. दर्भट.]

दर्म दर्म, अस्, or दर्मन्, आ, m. (fr. rt.
दॄ), Ved. a destroyer, demolisher; a tearer.
दर्यक दर्यक, अस्, m., N. of a man.

दर्व दर्व, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. दॄ), a
ladle, spoon (at the end of comp., e. g. पूर्ण-द्˚, q. v.);
the hood of a snake [cf. दर्वि below]; a Rākṣasa,
an imp, goblin; a mischievous man, a rapacious
animal, &c.; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people [cf. दार्व];
(आ), f., N. of a wife of Uśīnara; (sometimes written
दर्बा; cf. दार्वन्.)

दार्व, अस्, ई, अम्, wooden, made of wood; (आस्),
m. pl., N. of a people to the north-east of Madhya-
deśa, generally associated with the Abhi-sāras; (ई),
f., N. of several plants, = दारु-हरिद्रा, दारु-
निशा, Curcuma Aromatica or Curcuma Xanthorrhiza;
a particular species of collyrium extracted from an
infusion of the Curcuma Xanthorrhiza; a species
of pine, = देव-दारु; turmerick; a species of pot-
herb, Go-jihvā.
—दार्वि-पत्त्रिका, f., N. of a plant,
= गो-जिह्वा.
—दार्वी-क्वाथोद्भव (˚थ-उद्˚),
अम्, n. a particular kind of collyrium prepared from
an infusion of Curcuma Aromatica or Curcuma
Xanthorrhiza.
दार्व दार्व. See above.

दर्वि or दर्बि, इस्, f. (in later Sanskrit also दर्वी
or दर्बी, f.; acc. in Ved. दर्व्यम् or दर्वीम्), a
ladle, spoon; the expanded hood of a snake; (ई),
f., N. of a country.
—दर्वि-होम or दर्वी-होम,
अस्, m. an oblation made with a ladle; [cf. दार्वी-
हौमिक.]
—दर्विहोमिन्, relating to the preceding
oblation.
—दर्वी-कर, अस्, m. (scil. सर्प), a class
of snakes with expanded hoods, of which twenty-six
species are enumerated.
—दर्वी-सङ्क्रमण, अम्,
n., N. of a Tīrtha.
दर्वि दर्वि or दर्वी. See above.

दार्विका, f. a sort of collyrium prepared from
an infusion of Curcuma Aromatica; N. of a plant, =
गो-जिह्वा.

दर्वरीक दर्वरीक, अस्, m. a kind of musical
instrument; air, wind; an epithet of Indra; [cf.
दर्दरीक.]

दर्विदा दर्विदा, f., Ved. a species of bird,
(according to Mahī-dhara) = काष्ठ-कुट्ट, a sort
of woodpecker; (perhaps corrupted fr. दारु-विध;
cf. दार्वाघाट.)

दर्श दर्श, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. 1. दृश्), looking
at, viewing, seeing, perceiving, showing, having a
view, (generally at the end of comp., see अवसान-
द्˚, आदिनव-द्˚, आत्म-द्˚, तत्त्व-द्˚); (अस्), m.
sight, view, seeing, appearance, (generally at the
end of comp., see प्रिय-द्˚, दुर्-द्˚); the moon
when only just becoming visible, the new moon;
day of new moon; the festival of new moon; half
monthly sacrifice (performed at the change of the
moon by persons maintaining a perpetual fire); New
Moon or Day of New Moon, personified as a son
of Dhātṛ and Sinīvalī.
—दर्श-प, अस्, आ, अम्,
drinking the new moon oblation.
—दर्श-पूर्ण-
मासौ, m. du. new and full moon, the days and the
ceremonies which precede all other ceremonies.
—दर्-
श-याग, अस्, m. a sacrifice or ceremony on the day
of new moon.
—दर्श-यामिनी, f. the night of new
moon on which it rises hardly visible.
—दर्श-
विपद्, त्, m. the moon (‘as having the misfortune to
be hardly visible when new’).

दार्श दार्श, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दर्श), relating
to the new moon or the new moon sacrifice; (अस्),
m., scil. यज्ञ, the new moon sacrifice.

दर्शक, अस्, आ or इका, अम्, seeing, looking at,
a spectator; examining, searching; who or what
shows or displays or explains or makes clear; (अस्),
m. a door-keeper, a warder; a shower, exhibiter,
discoverer, one who points out; a skilful man, one
conversant with any science or art; (आस्), m. pl., N.
of a people.

दर्शत, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. visible, striking the
eye, beautiful; conspicuous; (अस्), m. the sun; the
moon.
—दर्शत-श्री, ईस्, ईस्, इ, Ved. of conspicuous
beauty.

दर्शन, अस्, आ, अम्, seeing, looking, (at the end of
comp., e. g. तुल्य-द्˚, देव-द्˚, धर्म-द्˚); show-
ing, exhibiting, demonstrating, teaching; (ई), f. epithet
of Durgā, ‘as showing the way or leading;’ (अम्),
n. seeing, observing, looking; sight, vision, observa-
tion; inspection, examination; perception; the being
or becoming visible; the act of showing [cf. दन्-
त-द्˚]; exhibition; appearance, aspect, semblance,
colour; visiting, visiting a sacred shrine, worshipping
in the presence of an image; going into the presence
of (e. g. दर्शनं कृ, to visit, to go into any
[]
one's presence; cf. पुण्य-दर्शन); a view or
theory prescribed in a system or book (e. g. शास्त्र-
दर्शनात्, in the manner prescribed in the Śāstras);
experiencing; seeing in the mind, mental or spiritual
vision, foreseeing, divining; contemplating; a vision,
a dream; apprehension, judgment; discernment,
understanding, intellect; knowledge, religious know-
ledge; opinion; intention; doctrine, demonstration,
a Śāstra, a N. applied to the six recognized systems
of philosophy (viz. 1. Pūrva-mīmāṃsā, usually called
Mīmāṃsā by Jaimini; 2. Uttara-mīmāṃsā, usually
called Vedānta by Vyāsa or Bādarāyaṇa; 3. Nyāya
by Gotama; 4. Vaiśeṣika by Kaṇāda; 5. Sāṅkhya
by Kapila; 6. Yoga by Patañjali; cf. तर्क); virtue,
moral merit; the eye; a mirror [cf. आ-द्˚]; a sacri-
fice, oblation [cf. दन्त-द्˚]; (ई), f. a kind of insect
(= तैल-कीट).
—दर्शन-पथ, अस्, m. ‘the path
of the sight,’ the range of sight or view, horizon.
—दर्शन-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—दर्-
शन-प्रतिभू, ऊस्, m. bail or surety for appearance.
—दर्शन-प्रातिभाव्य, अम्, n. surety for appear-
ance, bail.
—दर्शन-भूमि, इस्, f. the region or
range of perception; (with Buddhists) one of the
periods in the life of a Śrāvaka.
—दर्शन-लालस,
अस्, आ, अम्, longing to see, ardently desirous of
beholding.
—दर्शनेप्सु (˚न-ईप्˚), उस्, उस्, उ,
anxious to see.
—दर्शनोज्ज्वला (˚न-उज्˚), f. ‘of
brilliant aspect,’ great white jasmine.
—दर्शनोप-
निषद् (˚न-उप्˚), त्, f., N. of an Upaniṣad.

दर्शनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, visible, to beseen; observable,
perceptible, conspicuous; worthy of being seen, good-
looking, beautiful, agreeable, handsome; to be made
to appear before a court of justice, to be produced
in court; (अस्), m. Asclepias Gigantea.
—दर्श-
नीय-तम, अस्, आ, अम्, most worthy of being seen,
very beautiful.
—दर्शनीय-मानिन्, ई, इनी, इ, think-
ing one's self good-looking, vain, conceited.
दर्शयितु-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, wishing to show.

दर्शयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, showing, exhibiting, dis-
playing, a shower, exhibiter, director, instructor, show-
man, guide; (ता), m. a warder, usher, door-keeper.

दर्शयित्वा, ind. having shown or exhibited, hav-
ing made manifest.

दर्शयिष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, intending or pro-
posing to show or explain.

दर्शित, अस्, आ, अम्, shown, displayed, exhibited,
exposed to view; explained; seen, understood;
visible, apparent.
—दर्शित-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having
shown or explained or taught.

दर्शिन्, ई, इनी, इ, (at the end of comp.) seeing,
a spectator, looking, looking at, inspecting, observ-
ing, examining, perceiving, apprehending; knowing,
understanding; seeing or knowing (the hymns of
the Veda); experiencing, looking, appearing, having
an aspect; causing to see, showing, exhibiting, teach-
ing, causing to experience or suffer; [cf. अनीचि-द्˚,
अमोघ-द्˚, क्षेम-द्˚, पाप-द्˚, &c.]
—दर्शि-
त्व, अम्, n. the state of seeing &c.

दर्शिवस्, आन्, m. (perf. part. fr. rt. 1. दृश् without
reduplication; always at the end of comp., and usually
at the end of a verse), a seer, one who has seen, one
who sees or knows or understands (e. g. अर्जुन-
दर्शिवान्, one who has seen Arjuna; cf. दीर्घ-द्˚.)

दर्श्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. worthy of being shown
or exhibited; worthy of being seen, conspicuous.

1. दारु, उस्, उस्, उ (for 2. दारु see p. 410, col. 1),
liberal, munificent, giving, communicating, compas-
sionate; a giver, donor; an artist (in this sense
perhaps to be referred to rt. दॄ).

2. दारु, उस्, उस् or वी, उ (for 1. दारु see p. 408,
col. 1), tearing, rending; a tearer, breaker, destroyer;
(उस्), m., Ved. ‘the destroyer of cities,’ an epithet of
Indra; (उस्, उ), m. n. (usually n.), a piece of wood,
wood, timber; a block; a lever; a bolt; (उ), n. a
sort of pine, Pinus Devadāru; ore, metal in its
natural state; [cf. तरु, द्रु; Zend dāuru, ‘wood;’
Gr. δόρυ, δούρατα for δόρϝατα, δορήϊος, δουρ-ειο-ς,
δουράτ-εο-ς; Goth. triu, ‘tree;’ Old Sax. trio,
‘timber;’ Eng. tree; Slav. dre†vo, ‘tree;’ Russ.
dérevo, drova; Lith. dervà; Hib. doireach,
‘woody.’]
—दारु-कच्छ, अस्, अम्, m. n. (?), N. of
a district.
—दारुकच्छक, relating to the above
district.
—दारु-कदली, f. a wild uneatable plantain
(= वन-कदली).
—दारु-कर्णिन्, ई, m. ‘having
wooden ear-rings,’ a N. of Bhavila.
—दारु-गन्धा,
f. a kind of perfume (commonly चीडा).
—दारु-
गर्भा, f. a wooden puppet, a doll.
—दारु-ज, अस्,
आ, अम्, produced from wood, made of wood, wooden;
(अस्), m. a kind of drum.
—दारु-तीर्थ, अम्, n.,
N. of a Tīrtha.
—दारु-निशा, f. Curcuma Zanthor-
rhizon (= दार्वी).
—दारु-पत्त्री, f. a plant, =
हिङ्गु-पत्त्री.
—दारु-पात्र, अम्, n. a wooden
vessel.
—दारु-पीता, f. a plant, = दार्वी.
—दारु-
पुत्रिका or दारु-पुत्री, f. a wooden doll or puppet.
—दारु-फल, अस्, अम्, m. n. (?), Pistachio (tree
and nut).
—दारु-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, wooden, made
of wood (e. g. दारु-मयी योषा or स्त्री or नारी,
‘a wooden woman,’ a doll).
—दारु-मुख्याह्वया
or दारु-मुख्याह्वा (˚य-आह्˚), f. a lizard.
—दारु-
यन्त्र, अम्, n. a wooden puppet moved by strings.
—दारु-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a man.
—दारु-
वह, अस्, आ, अम्, bearing or carrying timber.
—दारु-
सिता, f. cinnamon in sticks.
—दारु-स्त्री, f. a wooden
doll; [cf. दारु-मय.]
—दारु-हरिद्रा, f. a species
of Curcuma, = दार्वी.
—दारु-हस्तक, अस्, m. a
wooden spoon or ladle.
—दारु-आघाट, अस्, m. or
दार्व्-आघात, अस्, m. the woodpecker.
—दार्व्-
आहार, अस्, m. a collector of wood.
दारु दारु. See col. 1. and p. 408, col. 1.

दारक, अस्, इका, अम्, breaking, tearing, splitting;
(अस्), m. a boy, son, child, infant; a young animal;
a village hog; the charioteer of Kṛṣṇa; (इका), f. a
rent, cleft, gap, chap; a daughter; a harlot; (औ), m.
du. a boy and a girl.
—दारकाचार्य (˚क-आच्˚), अस्,
m. ‘a preceptor of boys,’ a schoolmaster.
—दारिका-
दान, अम्, n. the gift of a daughter in marriage.
दारक दारक, दारण, &c. See p. 409, col. 3.

दारव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. दारु below), wooden,
made of wood, coming from or relating to wood.

दारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, tearing, splitting; (ई), m. (fr.
दार), a husband; a polygamist.

दारुक, अस्, m., N. of Kṛṣṇa's charioteer, who
was son of Satyaka; N. of an incarnation of Śiva;
(आ), f. a wooden figure; a doll, puppet; (अम्), n.
a sort of pine, Pinus Devadāru.
—दारुका-वन,
अम्, n., N. of a wood containing a famous Liṅga.
—दारुकेश्वर-तीर्थ (˚क or ˚का-ईश्˚), अम्, n.,
N. of a Tīrtha.

दारुकि, इस्, m., N. of Pra-dyumna's charioteer,
who was son of Dāruka.

दारुण, अस्, आ or rarely ई, अम् (perhaps not
directly fr. rt. दॄ, but rather fr. 2. दारु above),
hard, harsh (opposed to मृदु), rough, sharp,
severe (as speech); cruel, pitiless, heart-rending; ter-
rible, terrific, frightful, dreadful, fearful, grievous;
shocking, atrocious, dire; agonising, painful; intense,
violent, severe, great; (अस्, अम्), m. n. harshness,
severity, hard-heartedness, cruelty, horror, horrible-
ness; (अस्), m., N. of the plant Plumbago Zeylanica
(= चित्रक). दारुण at the beginning of comp.
or before a verb expresses excellence or superiority;
[cf. काष्ठ and see दारुणाध्यापक below.]
—दारुण-कर्मन्, अ, n. violent treatment (as of
diseases).
—दारुण-ता, f. harshness, roughness,
frightfulness, direness, severity, intensity.
—दारुण-
वपुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, of frightful shape.
—दारुणा-
कृति (˚ण-आक्˚), इस्, इस्, इ, of terrible or dreadful
form.
—दारुणात्मन् (˚ण-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ, hard-
hearted, cruel.
—दारुणाध्यापक (˚ण-अध्˚),
अस्, m. an energetic or indefatigable teacher; [cf.
दारुण above.]
दारुण दारुण. See col. 1.

दारुणक, अम्, n. ‘harshness,’ N. of a particular
disease affecting the roots of the hair.

दारुणाय, Nom. A. दारुणायते, &c., to act
harshly or cruelly, to be unmerciful.

दारुण्य, अम्, n. harshness (as of a sound &c.);
cruelty, dreadfulness, direness, severity, &c.

दार्वक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to or coming from
Dārva.

दारबलिभुज् दार-बलि-भुज्, incorrect form
for द्वार-बलि-भुज्, q. v.
दारिद्र्य, अम्, n. poverty, indigence.

दार्घसत्त्र दार्घसत्त्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दीर्घ-
सत्त्र), connected with a long continued sacrifice,
performing such a sacrifice.

दार्तेय दार्तेय, अस्, ई, अम्, leathern, made
of leather; (अस्), m. a patronymic from Dṛti, q. v.
दार्दुरिक, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to a frog, &c.

दार्भायण, अस्, m. a patronymic from Darbha;
(see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 102.)

दार्भ्य, अस्, m., Ved. a patronymic from Darbha,
applied to Śyāvāśva; [cf. दाल्भ्य.]
दार्वण्ड दार्वण्ड, अस्, m. a peacock.

दार्वन् दार्वन्, आ, m., N. of a son of Uśī-
nara; [cf. दर्वा.]
दार्वाघाट दार्व्-आघाट. See 2. दारु, col. 1.

दार्वीहौमिक दार्वीहौमिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr.
दर्वी-होम), relating to an oblation made with
a ladle.

दार्शनिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दर्शन), seeing far;
familiar with the Darśanas or philosophical systems.

दार्शपौर्णमासिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दर्श-
पूर्ण-मास), belonging to the Darśa-pūrṇa-māsa
sacrifice.

दार्शिक, अस्, ई, अम्, or दार्श्य, अस्, आ, अम्, relat-
ing to the new moon or the new moon sacrifice.

दार्षद दार्षद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. दृषद्),
ground on a flat stone (as meal &c.); stony, of
stone, mineral.

दार्षद्वत दार्षद्वत, अम्, n. (fr. दृषद्-
वती), N. of a Sattra.

दार्ष्टान्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, explained by an illus-
tration or simile; illustrated, any thing which is the
subject of an illustration or simile; suitable to be
used in illustration; one who uses an example or
simile as a proof.
दरीमन् (fr. rt. दॄ), Ved. destruction.
